locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:459-472 (the generic `bank` mechanism this new check imitates)
findings.description: The new self-report/findings consistency check (RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS-motivated, and a good idea on its own) is correct in WHAT it refuses, but its remedy text is not backed by the state write the remedy depends on, so following it fails a second time. The accompanying test (`test/rounds.jl`, "an audit lane's verdict must agree with its findings") only asserts that the refusal message contains the right lane names and that no claim ran — it never calls `gbg round rerun` with that exact invocation, so it does not catch that the suggested next step does not work.
findings.after: The diff adds: `bad = lane_verdict_contradictions(joinpath(dir, "findings")); if !isempty(bad) ... println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join([...], ",")); return 2 end`. This returns 2 WITHOUT ever calling `Rounds.bank` and without touching `rec["dead_lanes"]` or saving the round record. But `rerun(cfg, round, lanes)` refuses any lane that is not already present in the on-disk `rec["dead_lanes"]` ("a live lane is never re-run"), and a lane whose `verdict` merely contradicts its own `findings` count is schema-valid (the schema only enforces `verdict ∈ {CLEAN, CONCERNS}` and `findings` shape, not the cross-field CLEAN⇔empty rule), so `classify_lane` — the only code path that ever populates `dead_lanes` — returns `:live` for it, not `:dead`/`:rejected`. The generic `bank()` does the equivalent correctly: it writes `rec["dead_lanes"] = sort!(dead); save(dir, rec)` *before* printing its own "re-run only them" line, which is what makes that remedy work. The new code copies the message's wording but not the state-write that makes it actionable.
findings.before: Before this diff `audit_bank` had no lane-verdict check at all: after confirming `rec["instrument"] == "audit-changes"` it went straight to running the claim gate and the executable claims (`root = cfg["root"]; scratch = Preflight.scratch_dir(cfg, round) ...`).
findings.why_it_matters: A session that hits this refusal and follows the tool's own printed instruction verbatim — `gbg round rerun 2026-09-11-audit-changes-01 --lanes invariants,free-reader` — gets a second refusal: `rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank: invariants, free-reader (a live lane is never re-run)`, exit 2. There is no documented way out of this state through the tool; the only working recovery (deleting the offending findings/*.json file by hand so the file goes `:dead` — "absent" — on the next generic bank pass) is nowhere printed or documented. For an instrument whose whole selling point is closed-vocabulary, doctor-checkable process, this is a dead end presented as a fix.
findings.title: audit-changes bank's new lane-verdict-contradiction refusal prints a rerun command that is always refused
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Audit.jl: `println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join([replace(f, r"^\d+-" => "", r"\.json$" => "") for (f, _, _) in bad], ",")); return 2` (no `rec["dead_lanes"]` write, no `save(dir, rec)`) vs. src/CLI/Rounds.jl: `rec["dead_lanes"] = sort!(dead); if !isempty(dead); save(dir, rec); println(io, "bank: ... Re-run only them: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join(dead, ",")); return 2; end` and `bad = [l for l in lanes if !(l in dead)]; isempty(bad) || (println(io, "rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank: ", join(bad, ", "), " (a live lane is never re-run)"); return 2)`.

findings.description: A narrower guard (`v in ("CLEAN", "CONCERNS")` instead of `v isa AbstractString`) would have deferred any out-of-enum value to the generic bank's schema check as the file header comment already promises ("a file that does not parse, or carries no verdict, is the generic bank's to judge" — an invalid-but-present verdict string is not `nothing` and is silently swallowed here instead of deferred).
findings.after: `v = get(d, "verdict", nothing); v isa AbstractString || continue; ... (v == "CLEAN") == (n == 0) || push!(bad, (f, String(v), n))` runs BEFORE that schema validation and treats any string other than the literal `"CLEAN"` as if it meant CONCERNS for the purposes of the findings-count check — e.g. `verdict = "clean"` (wrong case) with zero findings is reported as `"clean" with 0 finding(s)", a contradiction`, mischaracterizing an enum violation as a self-report contradiction and routing it into the (also broken) rerun remedy above rather than the generic quarantine path that would have named the real problem.
findings.before: No such function existed; a malformed `verdict` value (anything outside the `CLEAN`/`CONCERNS` enum) surfaced only through `classify_lane`'s schema validation inside the generic `bank()`, which quarantines the file with a specific "invalid (quarantined)" reason.
findings.why_it_matters: The operator sees the wrong diagnosis ("its verdict contradicts its own findings") for what is actually an invalid-enum-value lane file, one step further from the actual defect and one more hop into the broken remedy in the primary finding.
findings.title: New lane self-report check treats every non-CLEAN verdict string as CONCERNS, silently accepting a malformed verdict the schema would otherwise reject
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Audit.jl: `v = get(d, "verdict", nothing); v isa AbstractString || continue` — accepts ANY string, not just the two enum members `catalog`'s own `instruments/audit-changes/schema.json` declares: `"verdict": {"type": "string", "enum": ["CLEAN", "CONCERNS"]}`.

locations: src/CLI/Audit.jl:43-45 (called before the claims and before Rounds.bank)
findings.description: The code comment says 'a file that does not parse, or carries no verdict, is the generic bank's to judge', but a parsed file with a string verdict and a non-array `findings` isn't handed on to the generic bank. RAN: `G.lane_verdict_contradictions` over a dir holding `{"verdict":"CLEAN","findings":null,"lane":"a"}` gives `null findings THROWS: MethodError`, and over `{"verdict":"CONCERNS","findings":"abc"}` it returns `[]` (no contradiction reported).
findings.after: `d = try JSON3.read(...) catch; continue end; v = get(d, "verdict", nothing); v isa AbstractString || continue; n = length(get(d, "findings", Any[]))` — `length(nothing)` throws, and nothing catches it inside audit_bank
findings.before: audit_bank ran the claims and then `Rounds.bank`, where classify_lane's schema validation quarantines a `findings: null` file: `return (:dead, nothing, sha, "invalid (quarantined): " * first(errs))`, then 'DEAD/REJECTED lane(s) — ... gbg round rerun'
findings.why_it_matters: An agent that returns `"verdict":"CLEAN","findings":null` is exactly the malformed lane the generic bank exists to classify. At base that produced exit 2 and a rerun hint. At head, `gbg audit-changes bank` dies with a MethodError backtrace, which Main's catch maps to exit 3 ('crash'). That exit code means a tool defect, not a lane to rerun. A string `findings` has the opposite problem: `length("abc")` counts characters, so a CONCERNS lane with a string findings value passes the check silently.
findings.title: A lane file with "findings": null now crashes audit_bank (MethodError, exit 3); base quarantined it as DEAD with exit 2
findings.evidence: Run output: `null findings THROWS: MethodError`; `string findings: Tuple{String, String, Int64}[]`. Main.jl:146-149 `catch err ... return 3`.

findings.description: The return-value fix removes a guard that nobody knew was refusing everything. The tool's own deploy guard flips from 'never deploy' to 'deploy on every built run'. The intent matches the base promise, but the flip is unannounced and untested.
findings.after:
+    # Documenter returns `nothing` unless `debug = true`, which is the frozen skip's own value, so a
+    # build that happened says so with `true`
+    return something(result, true)
findings.before:
check("gate check-docs check-consistency", GBGCodingTools.gate(cfg, "check-docs", "check-consistency"))
-    return result
findings.why_it_matters: docs/make.jl, which this diff does not touch, deploys through `result === nothing || deploydocs(repo = "github.com/GrigorySarnitsky/GBGCodingTools.jl", ...)`. At base, Documenter.makedocs returned `nothing` without debug = true, and the wrapper passed that through. So the guard refused EVERY build, frozen or not, and deploydocs never ran. The same holds for any consumer that followed the base seed's advice to "guard any deploydocs call on the value it returns". Input that used to be refused, a successful non-debug build, now reaches deploydocs, so the first CI run after this release publishes the tool's site and every consumer site guarded this way. The fix is correct against the base contract ("a make.jl deploys only when a result comes back"). But deploying from CI is a new side effect of a one-line return change, and neither the CHANGELOG nor any test marks it. No test covers the return value on the non-frozen path.
findings.title: makedocs now returns true on a built site, so the unchanged deploy guard in docs/make.jl passes where it used to refuse every build
findings.evidence: docs/make.jl:77-80: "# The wrapper returns nothing when a round froze the build ... result === nothing ||\n    deploydocs(repo = \"github.com/GrigorySarnitsky/GBGCodingTools.jl\", devbranch = \"master\", push_preview = false)". Base DocLints.jl: "Returns whatever `Documenter.makedocs` returns, or `nothing` when an open round ... a `make.jl` deploys only when a result comes back". The new comment in the ext: "Documenter returns `nothing` unless `debug = true`, which is the frozen skip's own value".

findings.description: A sentinel was removed from the rule ledger. Under the unchanged classification rule, at least CIT.DOI, MODULE_MAP and TEX.IMAGINARY meet the definition of `weakness` (a check could exist), or, for CIT.DOI, would cite the scan that already exists. The paired panel -> weakness moves on five TEST rules do not offset this: they concern different rules.
findings.after: +check = ["panel"]
findings.before: -check = ["weakness"]   (on each of HOME_ORDER, ONE_HOME, VARIANT_PAIR, MODULE_MAP, TEX.IMAGINARY, CIT.DOI)
findings.why_it_matters: The norm in policy/testing-protocol.md, which this diff does not change, reads: "A rule no program could ever decide is `panel`; `weakness` is reserved for the check that could exist and does not." Part of RULE.CIT.DOI is already decided by a program: the header of src/Scans/doi_crosscheck.jl reads "# SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK — RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE, RULE.CIT.DOI". RULE.DOC.MODULE_MAP's "carries no formula" and RULE.TEX.IMAGINARY's upright \mathrm{i} are text-decidable, and SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE already enforces part of HOME_ORDER (`# Arguments` before `!!!`, `# Fields` last). Recording these as `panel` marks them as answered with no program behind them, which removes them from the debt the rulebook tracks. The only reader of the field, test/schemas.jl:186 (`@test c in ("panel", "weakness")`), accepts either value, so no test notices. No computed result changes. What drops is the flag that says a mechanical check is owed. The panel itself is real: the doc-policy, latex-typesetter and citations-integrity hats read these rules.
findings.title: Six rules moved from `weakness` to `panel`, dropping the unpaid-check marker on rules a program can decide, RULE.CIT.DOI among them

locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:664-666 (rerun refuses any lane not in dead_lanes)
findings.description: Refusing a lane whose verdict contradicts its own findings is defensible under RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS. But the refusal was placed ahead of the one step that records a lane as re-runnable. The result is wider than the defect: a mislabeled CLEAN now costs the whole round instead of one lane's re-run, and a CONCERNS-with-no-findings that used to bank harmlessly as :empty now does the same. The fix would be to route contradictions through classify_lane as :rejected, or to write them into dead_lanes before returning.
findings.after: `bad = lane_verdict_contradictions(joinpath(dir, "findings"))` ... `println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", ...)`; `return 2` — before Rounds.bank, so rec["dead_lanes"] never gains the contradicting lanes, and rerun answers `rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank`.
findings.before: audit_bank went straight to the claims and `code = Rounds.bank(cfg, round; io)`; a lane file with verdict CLEAN and findings classified :live (banked), CONCERNS with zero findings and non-empty checked[] classified :empty (banked clean).
findings.why_it_matters: Concrete previously-valid input: an audit round whose lane file 03-invariants.json reads {verdict: CLEAN, findings: [one concern], checked: [...]}. At base `gbg audit-changes bank` banked the concern and exited 0. At head it exits 2 and prints `gbg round rerun <round> --lanes invariants`; that verb then exits 2 because `invariants` is not in dead_lanes (the open record starts with `dead_lanes = []` and only Rounds.bank writes it). The operator's only ways out are to hand-edit a lane file, which the first-sight sha regime exists to forbid, or to abandon the round. The new test asserts the hint's text but never runs the hinted rerun, so it certifies a remedy that does not work.

findings.description: Refusing CONCERNS with zero findings enforces a contract the base prompt already stated ('read as dead'). But the refusal bypasses the one mechanism that makes a dead lane re-runnable: `Rounds.bank` recording it in `dead_lanes`. It should record the contradicting lanes in dead_lanes (or route them through classify_lane as :dead) before returning. As written, the refusal is wider than the defect: it strands the round.
findings.after: "bad = lane_verdict_contradictions(joinpath(dir, \"findings\"))\n    if !isempty(bad) ... println(io, \"  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes \", ...)\n        return 2" — returns before `Rounds.bank`, so `dead_lanes` is never written; `rerun` then does `dead = Set(String.(rec["dead_lanes"])); bad = [l for l in lanes if !(l in dead)]; isempty(bad) || (println(io, "rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank: ..."); return 2)`.
findings.before: audit_bank went straight to the claims and `Rounds.bank`; a lane file with verdict CONCERNS and zero findings (non-empty checked[]) classified `:empty` and banked, and a lane recorded DEAD by `Rounds.bank` landed in `rec["dead_lanes"]`, which is what `rerun` accepts.
findings.why_it_matters: On the first bank of any audit round, where dead_lanes is still the String[] that open wrote, a contradicting lane makes bank exit 2 and prints `gbg round rerun <round> --lanes X`. rerun then exits 2 because X is not in dead_lanes. The round was bankable before this change. Now the only ways forward are to relaunch the whole audit workflow (every lane, anchors included, at full cost), to hand-edit a lane's self-report (which the frozen-instrument discipline forbids), or to abandon. The new test asserts only that the remedy string is printed, `occursin("--lanes invariants,free-reader", s)`, and never runs it against its own round's `"dead_lanes" => String[]`. The oracle therefore certifies a remedy that cannot run.
findings.title: audit_bank's new verdict refusal prints a rerun remedy that `gbg round rerun` refuses: a first bank has no recovery path
findings.evidence: Audit.jl:50 `return 2` precedes Audit.jl:74 `code = Rounds.bank(cfg, round; io)`; Rounds.jl:468 `rec["dead_lanes"] = sort!(dead)` is the only writer after open; Preflight.jl:670 `"dead_lanes" => String[]`; Rounds.jl:666 `rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank`; test/rounds.jl new testset writes `"dead_lanes" => String[]` and checks only the printed text.

findings.description: Under RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS it is reasonable to flag the CLEAN+n case, but a refusal that throws away banked evidence is wider than a warning or a normalisation (treat the verdict as CONCERNS when findings are non-empty). Combined with the rerun defect above, this case also has no working re-run path on a first bank.
findings.after: The same file is refused before anything is banked: "$f reports $v with $n finding(s) — its verdict contradicts its own findings", exit 2, with advice to re-run the lane, which replaces the file and its reported concerns.
findings.before: No bank code read the lane's `verdict`. A lane file with verdict CLEAN and one or more findings classified `:live` (Rounds.classify_lane), its concerns got ids `<round>/<lane>#n`, and `verdict_all_clean` was derived from the banked findings (`isempty(findings) && all(c -> c["exit"] == 0, claims)`), never from the self-reported verdict.
findings.why_it_matters: When a lane mislabels an inert field but reports real concerns with quoted before/after, the concerns now reach the bank only if a re-run happens to find them again, and an audit re-run is a fresh search with no memory of them. The base contract named only the CONCERNS-with-none direction as a contradiction ('A lane returning CONCERNS with an empty findings array is a contradiction and is read as dead'). The CLEAN-with-findings direction lost nothing at base, because the findings were banked and gated. Refusing it favours the self-report over the evidence, the reverse of what the bank does everywhere else.
findings.title: A CLEAN lane that reports findings is now refused outright; before, its findings were banked and had to be disposed
findings.evidence: base audit.js:85 names only 'CONCERNS with an empty findings array' as the contradiction; Audit.jl:77 `audit["verdict_all_clean"] = isempty(findings) && all(...)` ignores the lane verdict; new test writes `lane("CLEAN", 1)` and expects refusal.

findings.description: The contradiction predicate should apply only to schema-valid roster lane files (after classify_lane), or skip any file whose `findings` is not an array and any file not named `NN-<roster key>.json`.
findings.after: "n = length(get(d, \"findings\", Any[]))" runs over every `*.json` in findings/ before any schema check. A lane written with `"findings": null` gives `length(nothing)`, a MethodError that the VERBS wrapper rethrows, so the verb crashes (exit 3). A lane with `"findings": "none"` counts 4 and is reported as a verdict contradiction with the unrunnable rerun hint. The `filter(endswith(".json"), readdir(fdir))` also takes in `*.rejected.json` quarantine files and non-roster files, whose hint lane names (e.g. `invariants.rejected`) rerun never accepts.
findings.before: Every lane file went first to `Rounds.classify_lane`, which validated it against `schema["properties"]["lane_file"]` (findings: array) and quarantined an invalid one as `<name>.rejected.json` with status :dead, which put it in dead_lanes and made it re-runnable (exit 2).
findings.why_it_matters: An agent's malformed lane file used to go down the documented DEAD, rerun, re-bank path. Now it produces a crash, or a refusal whose remedy is wrong. The file's own comment says 'a file that does not parse, or carries no verdict, is the generic bank's to judge', but a parseable file with the wrong shape is not handed on.
findings.title: The contradiction check runs before schema validation: a schema-invalid lane file now crashes or is misreported instead of being quarantined as DEAD
findings.evidence: Audit.jl:10 `for f in sort!(filter(endswith(".json"), readdir(fdir)))`; Audit.jl:13 `n = length(get(d, "findings", Any[]))`; Rounds.jl:347/352 quarantine with `replace(p, ".json" => ".rejected.json")` beside itself in findings/; schema.json lane_file findings `items` (array).

findings.description: The mandatory makedocs wrapper's return contract changes from 'always nothing' (making the documented deploy-guard impossible to write correctly) to 'true on a real build, nothing on a frozen-round skip'. The change is well-motivated and thoroughly re-documented across DocLints.jl, ARCHITECTURE.md and the make.jl seed's comment, but it is still a return-value contract change on the one function every consumer's docs build calls, and it ships with no CHANGELOG entry in this diff.
findings.before: return result   [where result = Documenter.makedocs(; kwargs...), which Documenter itself returns as `nothing` unless `debug = true` is passed]
findings.why_it_matters: makedocs is the mandatory, public wrapper every consumer's docs/make.jl calls (WIRE.MAKEDOCS). Before this change its return value was `nothing` in BOTH the frozen-round-skip case and the ordinary successful-build case (since Documenter itself returns nothing unless debug=true) -- so any consumer make.jl written to the old documented contract ("a make.jl deploys only when a result comes back") could never distinguish a real build from a skip by the return value, and any `result === nothing || deploydocs(...)`-style guard would never fire deploydocs on an ordinary build. After this change a genuine build now returns `true`, a value it never returned before. This is the correct fix for a real defect, but it is a return-type/return-value change to a function every consumer's real, already-existing docs/make.jl depends on -- worth the release getting the CHANGELOG/version-bump treatment ARCHITECTURE's own release checklist calls for, which this diff does not include (no CHANGELOG.md hunk in the diffstat).
findings.title: makedocs' return value silently changes from always-nothing to true-on-success
findings.evidence:
diff --git a/ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl ... -    return result
+    # Documenter returns `nothing` unless `debug = true`, which is the frozen skip's own value, so a
+    # build that happened says so with `true`
+    return something(result, true)

findings.why_it_matters: This is a real bug fix (a fresh `gbg init` in a dev checkout previously left test/Project.toml pinned to a released tag instead of the dev source, per the added comment's own reasoning), but it mutates `envs` only in the real (non-dry-run) code path -- `envs` is computed once near the top of `init()` and is also what `--dry-run` uses to preview which `$e/Project.toml` files will be written, in code that returns before this new line runs. `gbg init --dry-run` on a fresh package therefore now under-reports what a real `gbg init` actually does: it will not show `test/Project.toml ([deps]/[sources]/[compat] GBGCodingTools)` in its preview, but the real run performs exactly that additional rewrite. A user trusting `--dry-run`'s listed writes gets an incomplete picture for this one file, and there is no test in this diff (test/rounds.jl and test/schemas.jl are the only test files touched) exercising either the fixed behaviour or the new dry-run/real discrepancy.
findings.title: gbg init's --dry-run preview no longer matches what a real run writes for test/Project.toml

findings.description: A deliberate, well-tested new self-consistency gate on `gbg audit-changes bank` that changes the CLI's exit-code behaviour for a round state that previously reached the claim-running stage.
findings.after:
function audit_bank(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout)
    dir, rec = Rounds.guard(cfg, round; io)
    rec["instrument"] == "audit-changes" || (...; return 2)
    bad = lane_verdict_contradictions(joinpath(dir, "findings"))
    if !isempty(bad)
        for (f, v, n) in bad
            println(io, "audit-changes bank: $f reports $v with $n finding(s) — its verdict contradicts its own findings")
        end
        println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ...")
        return 2
    end
    ... [claims now run only past this new gate]

    rec["instrument"] == "audit-changes" || (...; return 2)

    ... [claims run unconditionally once the round/instrument check passes]
findings.why_it_matters: A round whose lane JSON files were previously self-contradictory (CLEAN with findings, or CONCERNS with none) used to proceed straight into running the executable claims and the generic bank; it now stops at exit 2 before any claim runs. This is a new refusal for a shape of input the tool previously accepted at this step (whether the generic bank downstream ever caught it is a separate question this lane does not audit), and it is announced only in a docstring comment and a new test, not in CHANGELOG.md.
findings.title: gbg audit-changes bank gains a new exit-2 refusal path for input it previously ran to completion on

findings.why_it_matters: The commit message scopes this fix to 'a dev pin gets a path source rather than rev = "vdev"' — true only on the cfg["package"]["name"] != PKG_NAME branch, where test-Project.toml.seed hard-codes rev = "v{{tool.version}}" and needs the later render_project pass to correct it for a dev pin. The push!(envs, "test") line sits outside that ternary and fires on BOTH branches, including the tool auditing itself (cfg["package"]["name"] == PKG_NAME), where the seed text is the two-line "[deps]\nTest = ...\n" stub and a comment eight lines above states the design intent explicitly: 'the package under test IS the tool, so its test environment lists neither a tool entry nor a pin.' Sync.render_project/subenv_entries (unchanged) carry no PKG_NAME-self exclusion — they unconditionally inject a [deps]/[sources] entry for the tool into whatever env they are pointed at. So on a from-scratch bootstrap of the tool's own repo (gbg init with no existing test/Project.toml, the D15 fifth-consumer scenario this same commit's templates#2 note is otherwise about), the fix now also writes a self-referential GBGCodingTools dep+path-source into test/Project.toml, directly contradicting the adjacent comment's stated design and widening the fix beyond what the commit message describes. init has zero test coverage in test/*.jl (no test file calls init(...) at all), so neither the intended dev-pin fix nor this side effect on the self branch is exercised by the suite.
findings.title: Init.jl's templates#2 fix widens test/ sub-environment rendering to the self-consumer branch it explicitly excludes

findings.description: The contract was rewritten to match the code: the code already wrote `open` at base (Rounds.jl:632 at ed16027). Either §6.3 has to record `open` as the pre-disposition default (a MAJOR vocabulary change, with the frozen-at-bank wording reconciled), or bank should not write a disposition until one is recorded.
findings.after: "description": "open — the state bank writes for every REPRODUCED or EVIDENCED finding, before any disposition is recorded", "enum": ["open", "fixed", "refused", "escalated"]
findings.before: "state": {"type": "string", "enum": ["fixed", "refused", "escalated"]} — agreeing with §6.3: `disposition record | fixed | refused(reason ≥ 24 chars) | escalated(overturn_when)`
findings.why_it_matters: §6.3 is the closed-vocabulary table; CLAUDE.md says changing it is MAJOR, and §6.3 itself tells every consumer to audit its closed switches before adopting a widened enum. This change adds a fourth value only in the schema. The architecture row, which still lists three, was not edited, and nothing marks the change MAJOR. The same row says the record is 'frozen at bank (reproductions_sha)', and bank now freezes a record whose state is `open`. The base defect was real: `hunt_bank!` wrote `open` and then threw at validation on the first confirmed finding. But the fix bent the contract to fit the code rather than making the code honour the contract, and the new test certifies the widened enum.
findings.title: The disposition-state closed vocabulary was widened in the schema to fit the code; §6.3 still says three values

findings.description: The change lets a reading panel stand in for a buildable scan, contrary to the rule's own final sentence. RULE.TEX.IMAGINARY is the defensible case, since `i` as an index versus the imaginary unit is a judgment call; the other five are not.
findings.after: check = ["panel"]
findings.before: check = ["weakness"]
findings.why_it_matters: RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK says 'A rule no program could ever decide is `panel`; `weakness` is reserved for the check that could exist and does not.' Several of the reclassified rules are plainly decidable by a program. RULE.CIT.DOI ('Every reference carries a clickable DOI ... on its title') is a text scan; SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK already parses those bullets. RULE.DOC.MODULE_MAP's 'carries no formula' and RULE.DOC.VARIANT_PAIR's 'wrapper carries no display formula' are text or reflection checks. RULE.DOC.ONE_HOME's 'never one docstring per method' is a reflection count. Relabelling them `panel` converts owed checks into answers and shrinks the visible debt. test/schemas.jl accepts either value, so nothing notices. The five moves the other way (TEST.* panel→weakness) are the honest direction and are not flagged.
findings.title: Six program-decidable rules moved from `weakness` to `panel`, which by the rule's own text hides owed checks
findings.evidence: policy/testing-protocol.md:65-66 'A rule no program could ever decide is `panel`; `weakness` is reserved for the check that could exist and does not.'; RULES.toml:436 sentinel 'Every reference carries a clickable DOI on its title, `[*Title*](https://doi.org/…)` ...'; catalog/scans.toml names none of the six rules.

findings.why_it_matters: The code is unchanged: the post-build `check("gate check-docs check-consistency", GBGCodingTools.gate(...))` never had the skip. The promise was cut back to match it rather than the code being made to honour it. The rationale kept in the same sentence ('a red docs build keeps meaning something is broken rather than meaning a round is open') is now false for the post-build gate: a local build during which a round opens goes red for exactly the reason the design says must not turn it red.

findings.description: A justified fix that still changes a public return contract; noted so it is not released silently.
findings.after: `return something(result, true)` — docstring: "Returns what `Documenter.makedocs` returns, `true` when that is `nothing` — as it is unless `debug = true` is passed — or `nothing` when an open round ... froze the build"
findings.before: `return result` — docstring: "Returns whatever `Documenter.makedocs` returns, or `nothing` when an open round ... froze the build ... a `make.jl` deploys only when a result comes back."
findings.why_it_matters: The public binding's return value changes for every completed build. This direction is correct: the code was fixed to honour the base promise. At base a completed build returned `nothing`, the same as the skip, so the tool's own `docs/make.jl:79` (`result === nothing || deploydocs(...)`) never deployed. It is recorded here because a consumer make.jl that compared the result against `nothing` in the opposite sense would change behaviour, and the change belongs in the CHANGELOG as a contract change.
findings.title: makedocs now returns `true` instead of Documenter's `nothing` on a completed build
findings.evidence: docs/make.jl:79-80 `result === nothing ||\n    deploydocs(repo = ...)`

findings.description: The `something(result, true)` fix to makedocs's return value was correctly explained in three places (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md D9, src/DocLints.jl's docstring, templates/make.jl.seed) but not in the fourth and most concrete instance of the same fact: the tool's own docs/make.jl, which is the literal analogue of what templates/make.jl.seed renders for every other consumer.
findings.after: templates/make.jl.seed at head: "It returns nothing when an open round of a docs instrument froze the build (the instruments are frozen mid-round): that is exit 0, not a failure. A build that ran returns a value that is not nothing (`true`, or Documenter's document under `debug = true`), so guard any deploydocs call on `!== nothing`." docs/make.jl was not touched by this diff: it still carries the old comment (no mention of the new `true` sentinel) and the old `result === nothing ||` idiom rather than the now-recommended `!== nothing`.
findings.before: templates/make.jl.seed at base (and docs/make.jl, unchanged, still reads this way): "It returns nothing when an open round of a docs instrument froze the build (the instruments are frozen mid-round): that is exit 0, not a failure, so guard any deploydocs call on the value it returns." — and docs/make.jl:76-79: "# The wrapper returns nothing when a round froze the build: there is nothing built to deploy, and an unguarded deploy would publish the previous run's directory or none at all (WIRE.MAKEDOCS).\nresult === nothing ||\n    deploydocs(...)"
findings.why_it_matters: This diff's own ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl hunk changed `return result` to `return something(result, true)`, and templates/make.jl.seed — the seed every new consumer's docs/make.jl is rendered from — was correctly updated to explain the new sentinel and the `!== nothing` idiom. But GBGCodingTools is D15's 'fifth consumer': its own docs/make.jl is the one hand-maintained instance of this exact script (seeded once, then diverged, never re-rendered by sync) and it is the one the fix should have reached first. It still tells a reader the wrapper 'returns nothing when a round froze the build' with no mention of the new `true` value, and still guards with `===` rather than the corrected `!==` idiom — the tool's own copy of the fact it just corrected everywhere else is exactly the sample the house rule (RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP) says to sweep, and it wasn't. The guard still functions correctly by luck (`something` never returns `nothing` on the built path), so this is a stale/incomplete explanation, not a live bug — but it leaves the tool as a non-conforming example of its own freshly-stated idiom, in the one file most likely to be read as the reference implementation.
findings.title: docs/make.jl (the tool's own docs build) not swept when templates/make.jl.seed's makedocs-return-value contract was corrected

locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:452-473 (bank — the only writer of rec["dead_lanes"])
findings.description: The lane-verdict-contradiction check itself is a reasonable, narrowly-scoped addition (RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS: refuse before the executable claims run rather than after). But its user-facing remedy copies the wording of `Rounds.bank`'s dead-lane message without copying the state write (`rec["dead_lanes"] = ...; save(dir, rec)`) that makes that message's command actually work, and there is no `classify_lane` rule that would ever route a verdict/findings mismatch into DEAD/REJECTED on a later real bank pass either. A reader of the printed output has no way to discover this without reading Rounds.jl's rerun/classify_lane source — exactly the gap this lens is built to catch.
findings.after: audit_bank's new precheck prints the identical-looking instruction without ever calling Rounds.bank first: `bad = lane_verdict_contradictions(joinpath(dir, "findings")); if !isempty(bad) ... println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join([...], ",")); return 2 end` — it returns 2 immediately, before `Rounds.bank` (called later, at line 74, only on the path this branch skips) ever runs and could populate `rec["dead_lanes"]`.
findings.before: (new code — no prior version) Rounds.bank's own analogous message at line 471, which a reader would take as the model: `println(io, "bank: $(length(dead)) DEAD/REJECTED lane(s) — nothing frozen. Re-run only them: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join(dead, ","))` — printed only AFTER `rec["dead_lanes"] = sort!(dead); save(dir, rec)` on the line just above it, so the named lanes are already recorded as dead when the reader is told to re-run them.
findings.why_it_matters: A session (or the owner) that hits this refusal and types the exact command the tool just printed — `gbg round rerun <round> --lanes <the named lanes>` — gets a second refusal: `rerun` requires every named lane to already be in `rec["dead_lanes"]`, which only `Rounds.bank`'s own classification writes, and `classify_lane` has no rule that would mark a schema-valid-but-self-contradictory (CLEAN-with-findings or CONCERNS-with-none) lane file as dead or rejected in the first place — such a file classifies `:live`. So for the realistic case, the printed remedy is not merely stale prose but an unreachable command: `rerun` answers "refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank ... (a live lane is never re-run)" no matter how many times it is tried. The new test only asserts the string is printed, never that the command it names would succeed, so this went unnoticed.
findings.title: audit-changes bank's new lane-verdict-contradiction message tells the session to run a `gbg round rerun` that will always be refused
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Audit.jl: `println(io, "  re-run it: gbg round rerun $round --lanes ", join([replace(f, r"^\d+-" => "", r"\.json$" => "") for (f, _, _) in bad], ","))` immediately followed by `return 2` with no call to `Rounds.bank` on this path; src/CLI/Rounds.jl: `dead = Set(String.(rec["dead_lanes"])); bad = [l for l in lanes if !(l in dead)]; isempty(bad) || (println(io, "rerun: refused — not DEAD or REJECTED at the last bank: ", join(bad, ", "), " (a live lane is never re-run)"); return 2)`; and `classify_lane`'s only dead/rejected branches are absent file, changed-since-first-sight, unparsable JSON, schema-invalid, wrong `lane` field, or zero findings with an empty `checked[]` — none of which fires on a schema-valid lane whose `verdict` merely disagrees with its own `findings` count.
